# answer as plan JSON, frozen before the Java planner is deleted, for the Rust planner to be judged against byte for byte.
# Made with the identity oracle (rust/oracles/identity, its MANIFEST for the row key) by the same probe, the same two runs
# (A, B) over the same lanes on worktree-rust-port-phase0 at 1ea8fbf45 (core/src/main as of the merge of main at

# legend-lite-test-plan v11 over the product's v31). TestPlanner.planAhead was reached by no lane. Rows are keyed as
# the identity oracle's (model, query, doors, use), and a key here is a key there.
# A PLAN'S ID is the SHA-256 of its JSON's UTF-16 units, little-endian (the probe's, and rust/oracles/front's id), after
# MASKING run-specific values: one mask, the execution-trace comment's UUID (`executionTraceID" : "<uuid>`, the JSON's
# escaped quotes allowed) to 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000; planning reserves one under a verdict batch
# (testplan/ActivityComments). It applied 0 times in both runs: no frozen plan carries a UUID, so every id is the
# SHA-256 of exactly what Java's writer wrote. Stability: of the 73,411 keys in both runs, no plan id differs between A
# and B, in any row, before or after masking; within a run no key has two answers. A Rust planner reproduces a row when
# its writer's JSON for the question, masked so, hashes to the row's ids in order.
# WHERE THE TEXTS ARE. Every plan's id is here; the texts are for debugging a mismatch. A text store is in git when it
# is under 10 MB compressed (the largest frozen file in git is front/questions.jsonl.zst, 8.4 MB) and is not the
# database judge's (ruling 4: not ported at first); otherwise it is archived outside git, as the front oracle's full
# answers are, with its SHA-256 below and in plan-test-plans.sha256 beside it. Compressed with `zstd -19 --long=27`.
# plan-ids: model, query, doors, use (the identity oracle's key), then the execution plans' ids in order, then the test
# plans' ids in order (comma-separated; empty when none). 25,740 rows with an execution plan (25,741 plans: 25,694 rows
# through executionPlan, 46 projectPlan), 25,597 with a test plan (one each; query ids test 10,076, service 11,538, vs
# 3,551, fixture 432), none with both. The JUDGE a test plan was planned under is in its doors
# (testPlan@<runtime>,<judge>,<rules>...): HOST 17,651 rows (12,318 under lite's rules, 5,333 under the compatibility
# rules), and, MARKED as the database judge's, DATABASE 5,800 and BOTH 2,146 (both judges in one plan: the host's sides
# and the database's statement). The host judge's plans are what the Rust testplan is judged against (ruling 4); the
# database judge's cost nothing extra to freeze (the same runs: the corpus's database passes, the *_judge_database and
# *_judge_both lanes) and are frozen for when that judge is ported.
